title: Autocomplete under 50 ms
hook: A search box needs five suggestions for each typed prefix in under 50 ms. What data structure fits?
context: Search suggestion service; query frequencies change throughout the day
solution_brief: Use a trie and cache top five suggestions at each prefix node for O(L + 5) query work, where L is prefix length. This spends O(5 × total indexed prefix nodes) extra references. Batch frequency updates; a full sort at query time loses the latency budget.

steps.prompt: Which structure finds the prefix without scanning every query string?
steps.explanation: A walks the prefix in L characters. B costs a scan over all N strings. C has recency order but no prefix index.

steps.prompt: With prefix length L, what is trie lookup time before collecting suggestions?
steps.explanation: A follows one edge per character. B describes a scan of all N entries. C adds a logarithmic search that a character-edge lookup does not perform.
steps.bottleneck_note: The number of stored queries does not appear in prefix traversal time.
steps.context_note: The trie is already built in memory.

steps.prompt: How can the endpoint return top five without traversing a huge subtree per keystroke?

options.text: Store a precomputed top-five list at each prefix node
Sort every matching query on every request
Return the first five insertion-order leaves

steps.explanation: A makes collection bounded to five after lookup. B grows with the matching set. C does not produce the highest-frequency suggestions.
steps.bottleneck_note: Precomputation trades memory and update work for read latency.
steps.context_note: A popular prefix has millions of matching queries.

steps.prompt: What is the main cost of caching five suggestions at each node?

options.text: Up to five suggestion references per indexed prefix node plus update work
No update cost because the trie is immutable

steps.explanation: A scales with nodes and changes in frequency. B ignores pointers and node count. C contradicts live frequency updates.
steps.bottleneck_note: Measure indexed prefix nodes, not just the count of full terms.
steps.context_note: The team agrees to cache top five per node.

steps.prompt: The query log updates every second and traffic reaches a billion daily requests. What should be separated?

options.text: Batch ranking updates from the read-serving trie and atomically publish refreshed snapshots
Sort the full log for each keystroke
Mutate every ancestor node synchronously inside the user request

steps.explanation: A keeps reads predictable and permits slightly stale popularity. B scales with log volume per request. C makes user latency depend on update fan-out.
steps.bottleneck_note: Freshness can be seconds while the 50 ms read target stays firm.
steps.context_note: Read traffic now dwarfs frequency-update traffic.
